subject: Chemistry

mods.t: Atomic structure and the periodic table
Bonding, structure and the properties of matter
The rate and extent of chemical change

cards: AQA-8462.ISOTOPES

What is meant by ‘isotopes’? Answer in terms of subatomic particles.

[2 marks]

• atoms with the same number of protons
• (but with) different numbers of neutrons
Also accept: atoms of the same element
Also accept: atoms with the same atomic number
Ignore: atoms with the same number of electrons
AQA-8462.WEAK_ACID

What is meant by ‘a weak acid’?

[2 marks]

• (an acid which) is partially ionised
• in aqueous solution
Also accept: (an acid which) is partially dissociated
Also accept: (when dissolved) in water
AQA-8462.MASS_NUMBER

Define mass number.

[1 mark]

number of protons plus neutrons
Also accept: number of protons and neutrons
Not accepted: references to mass or relative mass of protons and / or neutrons
Ignore: protons and neutrons unqualified
AQA-8462.ACTIVATION_ENERGY

What is meant by ‘activation energy’?

[1 mark]

• the (minimum) energy needed for particles to react
• or
• the (minimum) energy needed for a reaction to occur
Also accept: the (minimum) energy needed to start a reaction
AQA-8462.BIOLEACHING

Describe what is meant by bioleaching.

[2 marks]

• (the use of) bacteria
• to produce leachate solutions (that contain metal / copper compounds)
AQA-8462.REDUCTION

What is meant by reduction?

[1 mark]
Loss of oxygen
AQA-8462.ALLOY

What is meant by an ‘alloy’?

[1 mark]

a mixture of metals
Also accept: a mixture of a metal with other elements
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_GROUP1_REACTIVITY

How does the reactivity of the elements change going down group 1?

[1 mark]
(reactivity) increases (down the group)
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_CHLORINE_POTASSIUM_IODIDE

Chlorine is more reactive than iodine. Name the products formed when chlorine solution reacts with potassium iodide solution.

[1 mark]

potassium chloride **and** iodine
Also accept: KCl for potassium chloride and I2 for iodine
Note: either order
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_NEW_ELEMENT_PEER_REVIEW

Tennessine was first identified by a small group of scientists in 2010. Suggest one reason why tennessine was not accepted as a new element by other scientists until 2015.

[1 mark]

(time needed for) peer review
Also accept: the idea that other scientists had to check the results
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_TRANSITION_VS_GROUP1

Tungsten is a transition metal. Potassium is a group 1 metal. Give two differences between the properties of tungsten and the properties of potassium.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• tungsten
• has a higher melting / boiling point
• is denser
• is harder
• is stronger
• is less reactive
• has ions with different charges
• forms coloured compounds
• can be a catalyst
Also accept: the converse for potassium
Also accept: the transition metal for tungsten
Also accept: the Group 1 metal for potassium
Also accept: is less malleable / ductile
Also accept: specific reactions showing difference in reactivity
Ignore: references to atomic structure
AQA-8462.R_4_3_3_HIGH_ATOM_ECONOMY_WHY

Why is it important to use reactions with a high atom economy in industry?

[1 mark]

• for sustainable development
• or
• for economic reasons
Also accept: to minimise use of limited resources
Also accept: to minimise use of energy
Also accept: to minimise waste
Ignore: references to yield
AQA-8462.R_4_10_4_HABER_SOURCES

The raw materials for the Haber process are nitrogen and hydrogen. Give the sources of the nitrogen and of the hydrogen used in the Haber process.

[2 marks]

• (nitrogen) air
• (hydrogen) natural gas
Also accept: atmosphere
Also accept: methane
Also accept: water / steam
AQA-8462.R_4_10_4_CALCIUM_PHOSPHATE_SALTS

Rocks containing calcium phosphate are treated with acid to produce soluble salts that can be used as fertilisers. Name the soluble salts produced when calcium phosphate reacts with:
nitric acid
phosphoric acid.

[2 marks]

• (nitric acid) calcium nitrate
• (phosphoric acid)
• (calcium) triple superphosphate
• or
• calcium dihydrogenphosphate
AQA-8462.R_4_2_3_FULLERENE_USE

Fullerenes are molecules of carbon atoms. Give one use of a fullerene.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• drug delivery (round the body)
• hydrogen storage
• anti-oxidants
• reduction of bacterial growth
• catalysts
• (cylindrical fullerenes for) strengthening materials
• (spherical fullerenes for) lubricants
AQA-8462.R_4_2_4_NANOPARTICLES_WINDOW_COATING

Self-cleaning windows are coated with a layer of nanoparticles of titanium dioxide. Titanium dioxide helps sunlight break down dirt particles and attracts water, so dirt is washed away by rain. Nanoparticles of titanium dioxide are used instead of fine particles of titanium dioxide for coating self-cleaning windows. Suggest two reasons why.

[2 marks]

• (nanoparticles)
any **two** from:
• have a higher surface area to volume ratio
• less (material) needed (for the same effect)
• more light gets through
Also accept: converse arguments for fine particles
Also accept: a thinner coating is needed
AQA-8462.R_4_2_4_NANOPARTICLES_LENS_COATING

Lenses in reading glasses often have a scratch-resistant coating that contains a hard substance. Nanoparticles of the hard substance are used instead of fine particles of the hard substance. Explain why nanoparticles are used instead of fine particles.

[2 marks]

• (nanoparticles)
• have a higher surface area to volume ratio
• (so) less coating is used
• or
• (with nanoparticles) a thinner layer can be used
• (so) more light gets through the lenses
Also accept: converse arguments in terms of fine particles
Also accept: (so) a thinner layer can be used
Also accept: less coating is used
Also accept: (so) visibility is not reduced (as much)
AQA-8462.R_4_6_2_HIGHER_PRESSURE_NOT_USED

In industry, the reaction is done at 450 °C and atmospheric pressure. Under these conditions the yield of sulfur trioxide is 86%. Suggest two reasons why a higher pressure is not used.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• the yield is already high
• more energy required
• risk of explosion is increased
• higher income from increased yield is outweighed by the extra expenditure
• increased cost of safety precautions
Also accept: requires stronger vessels
Also accept: requires thicker walls
AQA-8462.R_4_7_1_PETROL_FUEL

Petrol is burned in car engines. What general name is used to describe petrol when petrol is burned to release energy?

[1 mark]

fuel
Also accept: fossil fuel
AQA-8462.R_4_7_1_BROMINE_WATER_ALKENE_TEST

Describe a test for alkenes. Give the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• (test)
• add bromine (water)
• (result)
• (bromine water) turns (from orange to) colourless
Also accept: (bromine water) decolorises
Ignore: clear
AQA-8462.R_4_7_1_CRACKING_NAME_CONDITIONS

The heavy fuel oil fraction can be processed to produce smaller hydrocarbon molecules. Name the process which produces smaller hydrocarbon molecules from heavy fuel oil. Give the conditions used in this process.

[3 marks]

• (name of process)
• cracking
• (conditions)
• high temperature
• steam / catalyst
Also accept: a stated temperature in the range 300 to 900 °C
AQA-8462.R_4_7_2_ETHENE_AND_STEAM

C2H4 reacts with water vapour (steam). Name the compound produced when C2H4 reacts with water vapour.

[1 mark]

ethanol
Also accept: C2H5OH

Name the unsaturated hydrocarbon with the formula C3H6

[1 mark]
propene
AQA-8462.R_4_7_2_SMOKY_FLAME

Why does C3H6 tend to burn in air with a smoky flame?

[1 mark]

(because of) incomplete combustion
Ignore: insufficient oxygen
AQA-8462.R_4_7_2_ETHANOL_FROM_SUGAR

Ethanol can also be produced from sugar solution by adding yeast. Name this process.

[1 mark]

fermentation
Also accept: ferment(ing)
AQA-8462.R_4_8_1_FORMULATION

Some fertilisers are mixtures of different compounds in fixed proportions. What name is given to a mixture of different compounds in fixed proportions?

[1 mark]
formulation
AQA-8462.R_4_8_2_CHLORINE_TEST

Describe the test for chlorine. Give the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• (test)
• damp litmus paper
• (result)
• litmus paper is bleached
• or
• litmus paper turns white
Ignore: litmus paper turns red
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_SODIUM_ION_TEST

A student investigated an aqueous solution of a salt. The student identified that the salt solution contained only sodium ions and chloride ions. Describe a test to identify sodium ions. Give the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• (test)
• flame test
• (result)
• yellow (flame)
• or
• (test)
• flame emission spectroscopy
• (result)
• lines match sodium spectrum
Also accept: FES
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_CHLORIDE_ION_TEST

A student investigated an aqueous solution of a salt. The student identified that the salt solution contained only sodium ions and chloride ions. Describe a test to identify chloride ions. Give the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• (test)
• (add acidified) silver nitrate (solution)
• (result)
• white precipitate
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_FLAME_TEST_METHOD

Some metal ions can be identified using a flame test. Describe how to do a flame test using a metal wire and a Bunsen burner.

[2 marks]

• put sample on (metal) wire
• hold wire in (blue / non-luminous) flame
Ignore: references to cleaning
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_COPPER_II_TEST

Describe a test to show the presence of copper(II) ions in a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Give the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• (test) (add) sodium hydroxide (solution)
• (result) blue precipitate
• or
• (test) flame test
• (result) green (flame)
Also accept: blue-green (flame)
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_SULFATE_TEST_BARIUM_CHLORIDE

Sulfuric acid contains sulfate ions. Describe the test for the presence of sulfate ions in sulfuric acid. Give the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• (test) add barium chloride (solution)
• (result) white precipitate
Also accept: add barium nitrate (solution)
Ignore: (hydrochloric / nitric / sulfuric) acid
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_SULFATE_TEST_WITH_ACID

Describe a test to identify the presence of sulfate ions in a solution of potash alum. Give the result of the test.

[3 marks]

• add barium chloride (solution)
• add (dilute) hydrochloric acid
• white precipitate
Also accept: add barium nitrate (solution)
Also accept: add (dilute) nitric acid
AQA-8462.R_4_8_3_POTASSIUM_FLAME_TEST

The formula of potash alum is KAl(SO4)2. Give a test to identify the group 1 metal ion in potash alum. You should include the result of the test.

[2 marks]

• flame test
• lilac (flame)
Also accept: description of flame test
AQA-8462.R_4_9_2_GREENHOUSE_GASES_ESSENTIAL

Why are greenhouse gases essential for supporting life on Earth?

[1 mark]
(greenhouse gases) maintain temperatures on Earth (high enough to support life)
AQA-8462.R_4_9_2_POPULATION_CARBON_DIOXIDE

Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases. Explain why the increase in world population may have caused the increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

[2 marks]

• (increased population so) more energy required
• (so) more (fossil) fuels burned
• or
• (increased population so) more farmland required
• (so) more deforestation
Also accept: (increased population so) more transport required
Also accept: a named fossil fuel
AQA-8462.R_4_9_2_POPULATION_METHANE

Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases. Explain why the increase in world population may have caused the increase in the concentration of methane in the atmosphere.

[2 marks]

• (increased population so) more food required
• (so) more methane-producing food production
• or
• (increased population so) more waste produced
• (which) produces more methane on decomposition
Also accept: more use of beef cattle (in food production)
Also accept: more rice grown
AQA-8462.R_4_9_2_GLOBAL_WARMING_EFFECTS

Describe two potential effects of the increase in the mean temperature of the atmosphere at the Earth’s surface.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• melting ice
• rising sea levels
• flooding
• extremes of weather
• loss of habitats
Not accepted: acid rain
Not accepted: global dimming
Not accepted: references to ozone
Ignore: global warming
AQA-8462.R_4_9_2_SCIENTISTS_REJECT_THEORY

The mean temperature of the atmosphere at the Earth’s surface has increased. Most scientists think that this has been caused by an increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Give one reason why some scientists do not accept this theory.

[1 mark]

there may be other reasons for changes in the (mean) temperature (of the atmosphere at the Earth's surface)
Also accept: difficult to model
Also accept: the earth goes through cycles of temperature change
AQA-8462.R_4_9_2_CLIMATE_MODELS_DIFFICULT

Give one reason why it is difficult to produce models for future climate change.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• complex systems
• many different variables
• many alternative theories
AQA-8462.R_4_9_3_SULFUR_IMPURITIES_REMOVED

Petrol obtained from crude oil contains sulfur impurities. Explain why sulfur impurities are removed before petrol is burned in car engines.

[2 marks]

• (when burned sulfur impurities)
• produce sulfur dioxide
• (which) causes acid rain
• or
• (which) causes respiratory problems
Also accept: specified effects of acid rain
Also accept: specified respiratory problems
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_CALCIUM_MORE_REACTIVE_THAN_MAGNESIUM

A calcium atom is larger than a magnesium atom. Explain why calcium reacts more vigorously than magnesium with hydrochloric acid of the same concentration.

[3 marks]

• (calcium’s) outer shell / electrons are further from the nucleus
• (so) the outer electrons are less strongly attracted to the nucleus
• (so) positive ions are formed more easily
Also accept: converse arguments in terms of magnesium
Also accept: energy level for shell
Also accept: calcium has more shells
Also accept: (so) the outer electrons are more shielded from the nucleus
Also accept: (so) electrons are more easily lost
Ignore: calcium atoms are larger
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_POTASSIUM_WATER_OBSERVATIONS

Give two observations you could make when a small piece of potassium is added to water.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• (potassium) floats
• (potassium) melts
• (potassium) moves around
• potassium becomes smaller
• (lilac) flame
• effervescence
Also accept: potassium disappears
Also accept: fizzing
AQA-8462.R_4_1_2_GROUP1_REACTIVITY_EXPLAIN

Explain why the reactivity of elements changes going down group 1.

[4 marks]

• reactivity increases (going down the group)
• (because) the outer electron / shell is further from the nucleus
• (so) there is less attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron / shell
• (so) the atom loses an electron more easily
Also accept: (because) there are more shells
Also accept: (because) the atoms get larger
Also accept: (so) there is more shielding from the nucleus
Not accepted: incorrect attractions
AQA-8462.R_4_2_1_CALCIUM_CHLORIDE_FORMATION_ATOMS

Calcium chloride is an ionic compound. Calcium and chlorine react to produce calcium chloride. Describe what happens to calcium atoms and chlorine atoms when the ionic compound calcium chloride is formed.

[4 marks]

• each calcium atom loses two electrons
• (and) each chlorine atom gains one electron
• (so) one calcium atom reacts with two chlorine atoms
• (to form) Ca2+ ions and Cl- ions
• or
• (to form) calcium ion(s) and chloride ion(s)
Also accept: 1 mark for calcium atoms lose electrons and chlorine atoms gain electrons
Also accept: (to form) ions with full outer shells
Also accept: energy level for shell
AQA-8462.R_4_2_1_IRON_THERMAL_CONDUCTION

Iron is a metal. Describe how iron conducts thermal energy.

[2 marks]

• (thermal) energy is transferred
• by delocalised electrons
Also accept: heat is transferred
AQA-8462.R_4_2_1_SODIUM_OXIDE_HIGH_MELTING_POINT

Explain why sodium oxide has a high melting point.

[3 marks]

• giant structure
• (with) strong (electrostatic) forces of attraction between (oppositely charged) ions
• (so) large amounts of energy are needed to break the bonds / forces
Also accept: (giant ionic) lattice
Also accept: (so) large amounts of energy are needed to separate the ions
AQA-8462.R_4_2_2_ALLOYS_HARDER_THAN_PURE_METALS

Pure iron is too soft for many uses. Explain why mixing iron with other metals makes alloys which are harder than pure iron.

[3 marks]

• (the alloy / mixture has) different sized atoms
• (so the) layers are distorted
• (so the) layers cannot easily slide
Also accept: (positive / metal) ions for atoms throughout
Also accept: (so the) atoms cannot slide over each other
AQA-8462.R_4_2_2_THIOSULFATE_ACID_CLOUDY

Sodium thiosulfate solution reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. The solution becomes cloudy as the reaction takes place. The equation for the reaction is: Na2S2O3(aq) + 2 HCl(aq) -> 2 NaCl(aq) + SO2(g) + H2O(l) + S(s) Explain why the solution becomes cloudy.

[2 marks]

• sulfur (formed)
• (which is a) precipitate
Also accept: S / S8 (formed)
Also accept: (which is a) solid
Also accept: (which is) insoluble
AQA-8462.R_4_2_2_ZINC_OXIDE_EXCESS_OBSERVATION

A student produces pure crystals of zinc chloride by reacting zinc oxide with hydrochloric acid. The student adds zinc oxide to hydrochloric acid until the zinc oxide is in excess. Give one observation that the student could make to show that the zinc oxide is in excess.

[1 mark]

(zinc oxide) solid remaining
Also accept: (zinc oxide) solid no longer disappears
Ignore: references to colour / effervescence
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_EXCESS_ZINC_OXIDE_WHY

A student produces pure crystals of zinc chloride by reacting zinc oxide with hydrochloric acid. Why is excess zinc oxide used rather than excess hydrochloric acid?

[1 mark]

(excess) zinc oxide can be filtered off
Also accept: converse statements for hydrochloric acid
Also accept: separation / removal of (excess) zinc oxide is easier
Ignore: to ensure all the (hydrochloric) acid is used up
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_ZINC_CHLORIDE_CRYSTALS_METHOD

A student produces pure crystals of zinc chloride by reacting zinc oxide with hydrochloric acid. Describe how the student should obtain crystals of zinc chloride from a solution of zinc chloride.

[2 marks]

• heat (the solution) until crystallisation point is reached
• leave the solution (to cool / crystallise)
Also accept: heat (the solution) until crystals start to form
Also accept: heat (the solution) to reduce the volume
Also accept: heat (the solution) to evaporate (some of the water)
Also accept: if no other mark is awarded allow **1** mark for heat the solution to dryness
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_OTHER_SUBSTANCES_FOR_ZINC_CHLORIDE

Name two other substances that can each be reacted with a dilute acid to make zinc chloride. Do not refer to zinc carbonate in your answer.

[2 marks]

any **two** from:
• zinc
• zinc oxide
• zinc hydroxide
Also accept: Zn
Also accept: ZnO
Also accept: Zn(OH)2
AQA-8462.R_4_3_4_STRONG_AND_DILUTE_ACID

Dilute hydrochloric acid is a strong acid. Explain why an acid can be described as both strong and dilute.

[2 marks]

• (strong because) completely ionised (in aqueous solution)
• (dilute because) small amount of acid per unit volume
Also accept: dissociated for ionised
Not accepted: hydrogen is ionising
Not accepted: H+ are ionised
Ignore: pH
Ignore: low concentration
AQA-8462.R_4_4_1_CARBON_EXTRACTS_NICKEL

Nickel is extracted from nickel oxide by reduction with carbon. Explain why carbon can be used to extract nickel from nickel oxide.

[2 marks]

• carbon is more reactive (than nickel)
• (so) carbon will displace / replace nickel (from nickel oxide)
• or
• (so) carbon will remove oxygen (from nickel oxide)
Also accept: converse
Also accept: (so) nickel ions gain electrons
Also accept: (so) carbon transfers electrons to nickel (ions)
AQA-8462.R_4_4_1_PLATINUM_JEWELLERY_REASON

Platinum is used to make jewellery. Suggest one reason why platinum is used to make jewellery.

[1 mark]

any one from:
• unreactive
• appearance
• easily shaped
Also accept: does not react with air / water / skin
Also accept: does not tarnish
Also accept: aesthetic reasons
Also accept: malleable
Also accept: easily moulded
Ignore: references to cost
Ignore: references to hardness / strength
Ignore: references to melting / boiling point
AQA-8462.R_4_4_1_TIN_OXIDE_REDUCED

Tin (Sn) is extracted from tin oxide using carbon. The equation for the reaction is: SnO2 + C -> Sn + CO2 Which substance is reduced in this reaction? Give one reason for your answer. Answer in terms of oxygen.

[2 marks]

• (substance reduced)
• SnO2
• (reason)
• (SnO2) loses oxygen
Also accept: tin oxide
Also accept: (tin oxide) loses oxygen
AQA-8462.R_4_4_1_CARBON_EXTRACTS_TIN

Tin (Sn) is extracted from tin oxide using carbon. Why can carbon be used to extract tin from tin oxide?

[1 mark]

carbon is more reactive than tin
Also accept: tin is less reactive than carbon
AQA-8462.R_4_4_1_SILICON_POSITION_REACTIVITY_SERIES

The reactivity series sometimes includes non-metals such as carbon, hydrogen and silicon. Silicon can be extracted by reducing silicon dioxide with different substances. The equation for one possible reaction is: 2 C(s) + SiO2(s) -> Si(s) + 2 CO(g) Explain what this reaction shows about the position of silicon in the reactivity series.

[2 marks]

• silicon is less reactive than carbon
• (because) carbon displaces silicon (from silicon dioxide)
Also accept: converse
Also accept: silicon is below carbon (in the reactivity series)
Ignore: references to hydrogen
Ignore: (because) carbon reduces silicon dioxide
AQA-8462.R_4_4_1_OXYGEN_REDUCED_WITH_SODIUM

Why is oxygen described as being reduced in the reaction between sodium and oxygen?

[1 mark]
(oxygen) gains electrons
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_PIPETTE_AND_BURETTE_USE

Explain why the student should use a pipette to measure the dilute sulfuric acid and a burette to measure the sodium hydroxide solution.

[2 marks]

• pipette measures a fixed volume (accurately)
• (but) burette measures variable volume
Also accept: can measure drop by drop
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_TITRATION_INDICATOR_COLOUR_CHANGE

The concentration of an acid can be determined by titration. An indicator is added to an alkali in a flask. Name an indicator that can be used in this titration. Give the colour change of the indicator when acid from a burette is added to the alkali in the flask.

[2 marks]

• methyl orange
• from yellow to red / orange / pink
• OR
• phenolphthalein
• from pink to colourless
• OR
• litmus
• from blue to red
Also accept: if no other marks awarded, allow **1** mark for universal indicator turns from purple / blue to green / yellow / orange / red
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_ALKALI_ION_FORMULA

What is the formula of the ion that all alkalis contain when in solution?

[1 mark]
OH-
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_PH_WHEN_ACID_DILUTED

Explain what happens to the pH of an acid as the acid is diluted with water.

[2 marks]

• pH increases
• (because) the concentration of hydrogen ions decreases
AQA-8462.R_4_4_2_SALT_FROM_HCL_AND_KOH

Name the salt produced by the neutralisation of hydrochloric acid with potassium hydroxide.

[1 mark]

potassium chloride
Also accept: KCl
AQA-8462.R_4_4_3_MOLTEN_SODIUM_CHLORIDE_CONDUCTS

Sodium chloride is an ionic compound. Give one reason why molten sodium chloride conducts electricity. Refer to ions in your answer.

[1 mark]

the ions can move (in the liquid)
Not accepted: reference to moving / delocalised electrons
AQA-8462.R_4_2_2_SOLID_CALCIUM_CHLORIDE_NOT_ELECTROLYSED

Calcium chloride is an ionic compound. Solid calcium chloride cannot be electrolysed. Give one reason why.

[1 mark]

the ions cannot move
Also accept: the ions are in fixed positions
AQA-8462.R_4_4_3_ALUMINIUM_AT_NEGATIVE_ELECTRODE

Aluminium oxide contains the ions Al3+ and O2-. Explain why aluminium is produced at the negative electrode.

[2 marks]

• aluminium ions are positive(ly charged)
• (so) are attracted to the negative electrode
Also accept: (and) opposite charges attract
AQA-8462.R_4_4_3_CRYOLITE_MIXTURE_WHY

Aluminium is produced by electrolysing a molten mixture of aluminium oxide and cryolite. Explain why a mixture is used as the electrolyte instead of using only aluminium oxide.

[2 marks]

• mixture has a lower melting point (than aluminium oxide)
• (so) less energy needed
Also accept: cryolite lowers melting point (of aluminium oxide)
Not accepted: cryolite is a catalyst
Ignore: boiling point
Ignore: cost
AQA-8462.R_4_4_3_AQUEOUS_CALCIUM_CHLORIDE_NEGATIVE_PRODUCT

Calcium chloride is an ionic compound. Name the product formed at the negative electrode when aqueous calcium chloride solution is electrolysed.

[1 mark]

hydrogen
Also accept: H2
AQA-8462.R_4_4_3_COPPER_NITRATE_BLUE_FADES

Copper nitrate solution is blue. Suggest why the blue colour of the copper nitrate solution fades during the electrolysis.

[1 mark]

copper ions are discharged (from the solution)
Also accept: the solution becomes less concentrated
Also accept: copper ions are removed (from the solution)
Also accept: copper ions are used up (from the solution)
AQA-8462.R_4_4_3_ELECTROLYSIS_VERSUS_CHEMICAL_CELL

Electrolysis and chemical cells both involve chemical reactions and electricity. Explain the difference between the processes in electrolysis and in a chemical cell.

[2 marks]

• electrolysis uses electricity to produce a chemical reaction
• (but) cells use a chemical reaction to produce electricity
Also accept: voltage for electricity
Also accept: potential difference for electricity
Also accept: (electrical) current for electricity
Also accept: electrolysis uses electricity to decompose a compound / electrolyte
AQA-8462.R_4_5_2_HYDROGEN_FUEL_CELL_HALF_EQUATION

The reaction between hydrogen and oxygen releases energy. Reactions occur at the positive electrode and at the negative electrode in a hydrogen fuel cell. Write a half equation for one of these reactions.

[1 mark]

any **one** from:
• H2 -> 2 H+ + 2 e-
• O2 + 4 H+ + 4 e- -> 2 H2O
• H2 + 2 OH- -> 2 H2O + 2 e-
• O2 + 2 H2O + 4 e- -> 4 OH-
Also accept: multiples
Also accept: H2 - 2 e- -> 2 H+
Also accept: H2 + 2 OH- - 2 e- -> 2 H2O
AQA-8462.R_4_6_1_CHANGE_RATE_OF_GAS_REACTION

Give one other way of changing the rate of reaction between gases. You should not refer to pressure in your answer.

[1 mark]

• change the temperature
• or
• add a catalyst
Ignore: references to pressure
AQA-8462.R_4_10_1_DESALINATION_PROCESS

A different country has: very little rainfall, a long coastline, plentiful energy supplies. Suggest one process this country could use to obtain most of its potable water.
